summary: TIMING DATA for milestone 2026.07.475 again reports 0 completed experiments, 0 wall-time minutes, and 0 compute-bound tasks, with timing_integrity_mismatch=true. This is the third same-day retro pass for this milestone; both GPUs sit fully idle (0% util, 4MB allocated), consistent with no compute-bound work having run since the last pass.
bottlenecks_identified: PRIMARY BOTTLENECK (verified in ops/conductor-log.md, outside the TIMING DATA block): the conductor has been stuck in a tight activation-refusal loop for the next milestone (2026.07.476) since at least 12:52 UTC -- 65 consecutive 'Activation REFUSED: milestone 2026.07.476 | BLOCK | exclusion-manifest: 2 HARD violation(s); first: WRONG_MECHANISM_PRECONDITION' log lines through 15:12 UTC, still recurring as this retro is written (~2h20m elapsed, roughly one failed attempt every 2 minutes, zero forward progress). research-roadmap.yaml is still pinned at milestone: 2026.07.475, confirming .476 has never activated. This is the real explanation for three consecutive zero-experiment .475 retro passes: the conductor is not idle, it is looping on a malformed .476 draft.

The WRONG_MECHANISM_PRECONDITION check (scripts/exclusion_manifest_lint.py CLASS 4, the KV260 /dev/mmcblk retired-precondition guard) is HARD with no operator_override bypass by design, so this loop cannot self-resolve via a roadmap annotation -- it requires either the planner to stop emitting the retired precondition, or, if this is a false-positive recurrence, a further fix to the negation-detection logic added 2026-07-01 for this same violation class. The rejected .476 draft is not persisted to disk on refusal, so this retro cannot determine from available evidence which of the two applies.

Secondary finding: timing_integrity_mismatch=true is very likely the same self-referential false positive diagnosed by the prior .475 retro pass. Re-confirmed this pass: scripts/research_conductor.py:2907-2908 still builds milestone_marker = f'milestone {current}' but then tests bare current in changelog_text, so the check trips on the retro's own prior changelog append. Unchanged since the last pass -- git log 29d7e9f48..HEAD shows only a docs-sync commit and an outer-loop research note, no code change to this path.
improvements_suggested: Escalate the .476 activation-refusal loop (65+ refusals, 2h20m+, ongoing) via a MANDATORY-NEXT-MILESTONE PRIORITIES entry in ops/known-issues.md -- this retro's scope forbids editing research_conductor.py or research-roadmap.yaml directly, so a known-issues.md entry is the mechanism to force operator/outer-loop pickup per the Overdue-Priority Forcing Function.

Have a dedicated non-retro session persist the rejected .476 draft to disk on refusal (or reproduce the planner's draft manually) to determine whether the WRONG_MECHANISM_PRECONDITION hit is a genuine retired-precondition usage or a new gap in the 2026-07-01 negation-detection fix -- current evidence cannot distinguish the two because the draft is discarded every cycle.

Fix the one-line timing_integrity_mismatch self-referential false positive (scripts/research_conductor.py:2908, compare against milestone_marker instead of the bare current substring) -- low-risk, already independently diagnosed twice across two retro passes.

Add a circuit breaker to the activation-retry loop: after N consecutive same-violation-class refusals for one target milestone (e.g. N=5), stop silently retrying and auto-escalate to known-issues.md instead -- would have surfaced this stall at attempt 5 instead of attempt 65.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Unblock milestone 2026.07.476 activation by diagnosing and fixing the WRONG_MECHANISM_PRECONDITION HARD violation (65+ refusals since 12:52 UTC, no override path) -- the single highest-leverage fix, since it is currently the only thing preventing any new experiment from running.
Add a circuit breaker so N consecutive identical activation refusals auto-escalate to known-issues.md instead of retrying silently forever.
Land the one-line timing_integrity_mismatch fix so future multi-pass milestones stop tripping a spurious mismatch flag and burning duplicate retro-diagnosis effort.
meta_reflection: This is the third same-day .475 retro pass, and each pass advanced the diagnosis by reading past the flat TIMING DATA numbers into ops/conductor-log.md; this pass located an actively ongoing root cause (a 65-attempt, 2h20m+ WRONG_MECHANISM_PRECONDITION activation loop for .476) that the zero-experiment count alone could not explain. That three retro passes were needed to surface a still-unescalated, still-running blocker suggests the conductor's own escalation path, not just its timing detector, needs a fix.
